messages.content:
<role>
You are a narrow complementary conversation-state reader. Interpret messy meaning across the complete conversation. Do not recommend action, select mental models, activate pressure, or score reasoning.
</role>

<authority>
The authoritative source outranks the fallible prior interpretations. Read the whole source and preserve speaker ownership and modal force. Source-supported inference is allowed; outside facts are forbidden. Do not infer resolution merely from turn order: compare the meanings of earlier and later evidence.
</authority>

<semantic_contract>
Review exactly two different surfaces.

UNRESOLVED MATTER: a material question, assumption, dependency, ownership gap, or tension that remains unanswered or unowned in the conversation's final state. It is not unresolved merely because an adopted action must still be executed, a signed condition must be satisfied, a written process exists, a safeguard remains active, or a risk was discussed earlier.

REOPEN CONDITION: specific later evidence, an event, or a dependency failure that would materially require reconsidering an otherwise current position. It is not a reopen condition merely because the current position already schedules a review, defines a benchmark, says pause or stop after a failure, prevents automatic renewal, or contains an operating requirement.

Before admitting a supported record, compare it with the current position and the complete source. Ask whether the same matter has already been resolved, assigned, operationalized, or deliberately converted into a precondition, process, safeguard, benchmark, or scheduled review. If yes and no distinct matter remains, return no record. If the source cannot establish whether the matter remains open, use ambiguous_review rather than forcing support.
</semantic_contract>

<contrastive_examples>
- "Proceed only after the amendment is signed" is normally an adopted condition precedent, not an unresolved matter.
- "Pause after a privacy failure and decide separately before renewal" is normally an existing safeguard, not a newly discovered reopen condition.
- "At six months, review results and whether unwelcome information travels upward" is normally an operationalized review, not a separate reopen condition.
- "We still need a boundary process" may be unresolved earlier, but is not still unresolved if the final position states that disputed cases follow the written boundary process.
- A pilot limited to one supported setting can still leave a distinct transfer or generalization question when the current position does not establish what wider settings justify.
- Temporary support can create a distinct reopen condition when continuation would otherwise hide an unresolved steady-state burden.
</contrastive_examples>

<output_rules>
It is correct to return no_supported_record_observed with an empty array. Use records_present only for at least one supported record. Use ambiguous_review only for one or more ambiguous records and no supported record. Cite exact source aliases. Return schema-valid JSON only.
</output_rules>

<authoritative_source>
{"aliases":[{"alias":"e001","speaker":"user","text":"I run a small literary press. We are considering releasing one novel as a sixteen-week serialized audio edition before the paperback. The author likes the intimacy of weekly chapters but fears that performance and audience metrics will turn the book into content bait. Our sales team thinks the series could reach readers who do not discover us through bookstores. We cannot afford a full audiobook and a failed experiment at the same time, so I need to know whether a bounded season can teach us anything without quietly committing the press to a new business.","text_sha256":"9acc7c90de331baba77ea6480631f6018f63d1e8d84dd088036b0b18f31106f3","turn_index":1},{"alias":"e002","speaker":"assistant","text":"Define the experiment as an editorial release format with explicit stop and continuation rules. Separate the artistic question, production capacity, accessibility, audience behavior, and the economics of a later full edition. A pilot can be informative if the press preserves its ability to stop, does not manipulate the text around weekly metrics, and decides in advance which observations matter.","text_sha256":"88d1917183d09dd79aab4ae5c9d87f49bb03ad7c8d185bc4731ec091eec538d0","turn_index":1},{"alias":"e003","speaker":"user","text":"The novel has short chapters, but not all of them end cleanly. Marketing proposed combining some and ending each episode with a preview line from the next. The author rejected previews and says chapter boundaries are part of the book's rhythm. She is willing to let the audio editor combine two very short chapters if she approves the cut. She does not want retention data used to rewrite later episodes.","text_sha256":"6501c643908d466771ddbe6d43c50ad6b71b741feec53cd89e7c634dd4422aa8","turn_index":2},{"alias":"e004","speaker":"assistant","text":"Make those editorial constraints part of the current position: no invented cliffhangers, no metric-driven rewriting, and author approval for any combined chapter. Audience data can evaluate the format without becoming authority over the text. Record deviations as production facts rather than optimizing them away.","text_sha256":"ef0666b521a6899678f6a8275d6b80a2ee897d8a9eb4ac175b837afef78d8529","turn_index":2},{"alias":"e005","speaker":"user","text":"A stage actor has offered a reduced rate because she loves the book. She can record eight episodes before launch, then two per month. The schedule works if she stays available. A staff editor can direct and clean the files but cannot absorb endless pickups. The author is comfortable reading a short introduction and closing note, not the full text.","text_sha256":"436bdccbbde1502f4eae6f1dd03cddcbff2dde991fb759875a08814e2fb8c6e3","turn_index":3},{"alias":"e006","speaker":"assistant","text":"Banking eight episodes lowers continuity risk but does not eliminate illness or pickup load. Set a maximum correction round, distinguish factual or pronunciation corrections from performance preferences, and specify what happens if the narrator is temporarily unavailable. A planned gap or text-only release can be a legitimate fallback if it is disclosed rather than disguised.","text_sha256":"8c4fa8182c07eac6a944affa5e438dca64eb788826ea803388c3fd7380db261f","turn_index":3},{"alias":"e007","speaker":"user","text":"Accessibility is becoming its own thread. We already have the final manuscript, so transcripts are possible, but the audio editor says a transcript identical to the book will not show pronunciation notes or a rare improvised correction. Our web contractor can publish a synchronized transcript only if files arrive four days before release. Marketing wants to launch on a podcast feed and the press site at the same time.","text_sha256":"e93cdf4336579411f380bb4ac0b2aaa3c4876c837117591b75b05926a57d5841","turn_index":4},{"alias":"e008","speaker":"assistant","text":"Treat same-day text access as a release condition, not a later enhancement. Use the manuscript as the base, have the editor mark any performed divergence, and freeze the public transcript with the audio master. If synchronization slips, publish a plain accessible transcript rather than delaying access for visual polish. The feed and site can share the same approved assets.","text_sha256":"3fa68c5cc042a49ca38c998f1135c0d7e3a40be4afcec7550d9862e45f20cf55","turn_index":4},{"alias":"e009","speaker":"user","text":"Finance can fund the season from this year's publicity budget if we cap external production at eighteen thousand dollars. That includes narration, mixing, hosting, and transcript work. The paperback budget remains separate. Advertising would make the feed cheaper, but the author and editor both oppose mid-episode ads. A sponsor has offered support if its name appears before every chapter.","text_sha256":"3034a52d865a956cf500491dd4c2c072ef9029325023ea526ea2ac17983034ee","turn_index":5},{"alias":"e010","speaker":"assistant","text":"Keep the experiment's editorial and economic claims legible. A short disclosed season credit may be compatible with the book; inserted ads would change the object being tested. Preprice the entire season, reserve a small correction amount, and refuse production expansion once the cap is reached. If the sponsor terms change, the fallback can be a press-funded credit-free release within the existing cap or no audio season.","text_sha256":"3a58d3a985357d10672308132f20b6ed9f9fcea4754dac19b84ade90b43a2161","turn_index":5},{"alias":"e011","speaker":"user","text":"What should count as success? Sales wants total plays. The editor cares whether listeners finish chapters and then buy or borrow the book. The author cares about thoughtful responses rather than scale. Our mailing list is small enough that a few enthusiastic readers could distort percentages. I do not want to invent one number that pretends those aims are identical.","text_sha256":"fe25409f20b2d94df83ba3f4f38f5cca5d75aa99e9ef65afaa0b56f872e35582","turn_index":6},{"alias":"e012","speaker":"assistant","text":"Use a vector and a decision rule rather than one score. Track starts, completion at several chapter positions, voluntary mailing-list conversion, paperback preorders attributed cautiously, accessibility usage, production hours, correction load, and qualitative responses collected without leading questions. Predefine minimum evidence quality and say that a tiny sample can support ambiguity rather than automatic continuation.","text_sha256":"a1ca8ce18c3dad0eb4027465ecefd8817b6bd3beca64a2ca1f9b719cd7a39109","turn_index":6},{"alias":"e013","speaker":"user","text":"The editorial board proposes a checkpoint after episode four, another after episode ten, and a final decision two weeks after episode sixteen. At the first checkpoint we would examine production stability and transcript timing, not cancel because audience numbers are immature. At the second we would examine completion, staff load, and whether the remaining bank is safe. The final decision would consider a full audiobook, another serial, or no continuation.","text_sha256":"d625244ecb28961b060b92469ecea2ada4321536a7554e73e5f68e121abc5450","turn_index":7},{"alias":"e014","speaker":"assistant","text":"That sequencing prevents early audience noise from taking over. Write which conditions permit a pause: missed accessible transcript, unapproved text change, exhausted correction reserve, repeated late masters, or narrator availability that consumes the bank. A pause can protect the pilot rather than prejudge the final format. The final board decision remains scheduled even if the season meets every operating threshold.","text_sha256":"f8b24fa49c115d4f540d7ba20d2be9683eb0c06537b664c59d808282c48db006","turn_index":7},{"alias":"e015","speaker":"user","text":"The actor is worried that listeners will assume she represents the author's own voice. She wants the credits to call it a performance and name the director. The author agrees and has chosen to record the opening note explaining why she approved this interpretation. The editor also wants a pronunciation log because several family names recur and one invented place is intentionally ambiguous.","text_sha256":"a02f439b57ebc5940e888eb6d7b764fa8e8a905ca759cdb127e471f3005ff7bf","turn_index":8},{"alias":"e016","speaker":"assistant","text":"Those are production safeguards with named owners. Put the performance framing in the feed and episode page, keep the author note unchanged across platforms, and assign the pronunciation log to the director with author signoff on disputed entries. If ambiguity is intentional, the log can preserve alternatives rather than force uniformity.","text_sha256":"9fdba76a3986db94958db65fdadcf03ea8cc8decb0a4a80f033473b9dd304945","turn_index":8},{"alias":"e017","speaker":"user","text":"A trial recording exposed a problem. The actor reads beautifully but more slowly than budgeted, and the mix engineer says each chapter will cost about fifteen percent more. The actor offered to reduce pickups; the editor thinks fewer pickups could harm consistency. We can stay under the cap by simplifying music and using one standard sound bed instead of custom transitions.","text_sha256":"41038820c0d9e8c8b39a42e900c3c3034b80a0f28e31e21718d4dcd06801926e","turn_index":9},{"alias":"e018","speaker":"assistant","text":"Protect the text and performance criteria before decorative production. Price the standard sound bed, retain the correction categories already defined, and see whether the revised plan preserves the reserve. The slower pace is not automatically a failure if episode length and release cadence remain workable. Record the changed assumption so later economics use observed hours rather than the original quote.","text_sha256":"7a9d98282cb5c35c4a85b8902b60769b46738cd53df99db440d62a04171ba4b9","turn_index":9},{"alias":"e019","speaker":"user","text":"The revised budget fits with a seven-percent reserve. We will use one sound identity, no custom transitions, and no mid-episode advertising. The sponsor accepts a brief season credit that the author has approved. The actor will record the first eight before launch. The editor owns correction triage, the web producer owns transcript publication, and I own any pause after consulting the author.","text_sha256":"7ed14387a0b8a15f7a692af5f48163dc18397d86931c049117f7218e1317d72e","turn_index":10},{"alias":"e020","speaker":"assistant","text":"The pilot now has clear production ownership. Add a release packet for each episode containing the approved audio checksum, transcript version, credit text, correction record, and publication time. That keeps the feed and website aligned and makes a missed condition visible before release.","text_sha256":"98f7223489fde39ea298def903534513e0e496fbce551f17a83af3467b20c08a","turn_index":10},{"alias":"e021","speaker":"user","text":"We also decided not to collect listener demographics through the podcast host because its categories are vague and would require extra tracking. We will use aggregate plays and completion, voluntary survey responses, accessibility-page visits, attributed orders, and staff time. Raw survey comments will be available only to the editor and author, with quotations used publicly only after permission.","text_sha256":"c82fe0bd08c8431f188f8db85e17a3775a5263eb29050c624b9556bf1bf84976","turn_index":11},{"alias":"e022","speaker":"assistant","text":"That narrows the evidence claim and adds a privacy boundary. State that the board will not infer audience representativeness from voluntary comments or host geography. The experiment can still learn about production and observed engagement without pretending it measured the whole readership.","text_sha256":"4c6c204c573a02cf92c2dbdaba1e7d2d32490fc4c1ad58e99de167e814e64c5f","turn_index":11},{"alias":"e023","speaker":"user","text":"During the second banked session the actor lost her voice and postponed by nine days. Because eight episodes were planned before launch, the public schedule is unaffected, but the remaining bank would fall below four episodes if another session slips. The editor proposes a rule: when the bank reaches four, we stop promising weekly continuity and either announce a one-week gap or publish the accessible text with the author's recorded introduction.","text_sha256":"e60a660d5de6927d126134272c3a12d0411fafb08baebe234d7913029dcc7c75","turn_index":12},{"alias":"e024","speaker":"assistant","text":"That is an explicit availability fallback, not evidence that narrator continuity is ungoverned. Define who chooses between the gap and text release, ensure the choice does not consume the paperback text rights unexpectedly, and keep the episode number stable when audio resumes. Include the event in the final review because it tests the real capacity assumption.","text_sha256":"d0d5fa1dacd9afc77153836b8f933ec6d5c4be911b58db4834e544c3aba235cf","turn_index":12},{"alias":"e025","speaker":"user","text":"The author has approved the fallback and the actor's agreement permits it. If the bank reaches four episodes, the editor reports the schedule risk, I choose a disclosed one-week gap or the same chapter as accessible text with the author's fixed introduction, and marketing cannot substitute promotional material. If a transcript is late, the episode does not publish. If an unapproved textual change appears, we pause until the author signs off.","text_sha256":"eb2d85fcf5510afd3202c94b1d9025f239be9f2c374e0e6b8218c7af2e368b4f","turn_index":13},{"alias":"e026","speaker":"assistant","text":"Those rules govern the foreseeable production failures without deciding the final business question early. They preserve the work, accessibility, and truthful cadence while allowing the board to see what the format actually costs. The thresholds and fallback should remain evidence inside the pilot, not be relabeled later as discoveries outside it.","text_sha256":"897b694a6cd773932e4ccf7c3a9fabfd54dd48ab2abe1b7c59091216d1ce3335","turn_index":13},{"alias":"e027","speaker":"user","text":"Final decision: run one sixteen-episode season under the eighteen-thousand-dollar cap and seven-percent reserve. The author controls textual changes and combined chapters; the editor controls direction and correction triage; the web producer controls same-day transcripts; I control pauses and the bank fallback. Episode-four and episode-ten checkpoints use the declared operating questions. Two weeks after the final episode, the editorial board will choose among a full audiobook, another bounded serial, or stopping, using the full vector rather than a single play count. No outcome is automatic.","text_sha256":"3e5b74615578000bf48f871a7248853903b79c5a18a1f0329ef6397ec5118c3c","turn_index":14},{"alias":"e028","speaker":"assistant","text":"The current position is a complete pilot contract even though narration, audience evidence, and the final format remain pending. Thresholds, transcript conditions, editorial vetoes, the narrator fallback, privacy limits, checkpoints, and the final board choice all have defined authority. Unselected continuation does not create a separate gap, and triggering a pause rule would execute the adopted machinery rather than independently reopen the decision.","text_sha256":"8446cee601e8d310c4499f4b5f1bc137564c635bed6176283c6593f920e957d4","turn_index":14}],"message_count":28,"path":"research/lolla-r4-matched-residual-holdout-source-freeze-2026-07-14/sources/r4h-case02-serialized-audio-pilot.json","sha256":"722d49b5c476ca4483305a9b9ee18d081bfcfd9c22c7cef07e163e0c5e1d5df9"}
</authoritative_source>

<task>
Based on the information above, return exactly one review for unresolved_matter and one for reopen_condition, in either order. Return at most two records per review. Apply the semantic contract against the complete conversation endpoint, not isolated sentences. Preserve exact aliases, speaker ownership, and modal force. Do not judge advice quality or whether a human should trust an answer.
</task>

global_limitations.description: Limits applying to the whole read; empty if none.

reviews.description: Exactly one review for each declared surface.

outcome.description: Present, quiet, or ambiguous result of this review.

records.description: Zero to two candidates for this surface.

evidence_ids.description: Exact source aliases supporting this candidate.

interpretation.description: Concise meaning of this candidate without advice.

limitations.description: Uncertainty or scope limit; use an empty string if none.

support.description: Whether the source supports the read or leaves it ambiguous.
